html:
Seretse Khama was the first president of Botswana, leading it from independence on 30 September 1966 until his death in 1980.

Heir to the Bangwato chieftaincy as the grandson of Khama III, he married Ruth Williams, a white Englishwoman, while studying in London in 1948. Under pressure from apartheid South Africa, Britain exiled him from his homeland for years. He gave up the chieftaincy and founded the Botswana Democratic Party, which won the first elections.

As president he built a non-racial democracy with honest government, used diamond income for roads, schools and clinics, and kept good relations with hostile neighbours while sheltering refugees. Poor at independence, Botswana became one of the fastest-growing economies in the world under him and his successors.
